name: Eshtemoa
overview: Eshtemoa was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the Maacathite and noted as the grandson of Hodiah. His mention in Scripture is brief, focusing primarily on his tribal affiliation and lineage without additional narrative details. This concise record situates him within the genealogical framework important to Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Eshtemoa means "[place where oracle is] heard," indicating a possible connection to a location known for divine communication. This proper name was not given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew designation tied to spiritual hearing or revelation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eshtemoa as the grandson of Hodiah, establishing a direct familial link within the tribe of Judah. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented, limiting our understanding to this single generational connection.
scriptureSignificance: Eshtemoa's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of Judah, emphasizing the preservation of tribal identities and lineages important for God's covenant people. His designation as the Maacathite and grandson of Hodiah highlights the interconnectedness of families within the tribe. Though not elaborated upon, his mention contributes to the broader biblical narrative of God's faithfulness in maintaining His chosen line.
